locators: Page 1, Indications for use
text: US labeling indicates Neuroform Atlas with neurovascular embolic coils for patients age 18 or older with wide-neck intracranial saccular aneurysms arising from a 2.0-4.5 mm parent vessel that are not amenable to surgical clipping; wide neck is defined as neck at least 4 mm or dome-to-neck ratio below 2.

locators: Page 1, Contraindications
text: US labeling contraindicates Neuroform Atlas in patients for whom antiplatelet and/or anticoagulation therapy is contraindicated.

locators: Page 1, Warnings, fifth bullet
text: Select stent length to maintain at least 4 mm beyond each side of the aneurysm neck along the parent vessel; the labeling states that the stent is not designed for an aneurysm neck longer than 22 mm.

locators: Page 1, Cautions / precautions, fifth bullet
text: The labeling states that Neuroform Atlas may foreshorten by up to 6.3% after deployment.

locators: Page 1, Cautions / precautions, sixth and seventh bullets
text: The coiling microcatheter maximum outer diameter should not exceed that of the stent-delivery microcatheter; standard interventional devices with distal tips greater than 1.8 F may not pass through the stent interstices.

locators: Page 1, Magnetic Resonance Imaging Safety Information
text: The implant is MR Conditional immediately after placement at 1.5 or 3.0 T, with maximum spatial gradient 2500 G/cm, whole-body averaged SAR 2 W/kg, and head-averaged SAR 3.2 W/kg; the stated maximum temperature rise applies after 15 minutes of continuous scanning under those conditions.

locators: PDF page 1, HDE statement beneath the title
text: The River Stent System is a Humanitarian Device authorized by Federal law for use in the treatment of idiopathic intracranial hypertension in adult patients who have failed medical therapy; the labeling states that the effectiveness of the device for this use has not been demonstrated.

locators: PDF page 4, section 3 Indications for Use
text: US labeling indicates the River Stent System for stenting of the venous sinus in adults (22 years or older) with idiopathic intracranial hypertension who have failed medical therapy, have a significant venous sinus stenosis (>50% stenosis and pressure gradient >=8 mmHg), and have an upstream venous sinus diameter between 5 mm and 8.5 mm; patients must also meet at least one of two further criteria: (1) intractable headache (HIT-6 score >59) with papilledema or a history of papilledema and at least 6 months of failed medical therapy, with obese patients (BMI >=30) also having completed at least 6 months of a weight-management program without adequate relief, or (2) moderate to severe papilledema (Frisen grade >=2), transient visual obscuration, or sixth nerve palsy after failed medical therapy with the treating ophthalmologist judging vision to be at risk.

locators: PDF page 4, section 4 Contraindications (first two bullets)
PDF page 5, section 4 Contraindications (remaining bullets)
text: US labeling contraindicates the River Stent System in patients in whom anticoagulant, antiplatelet, or thrombolytic drugs are contraindicated; patients with a thrombophilic disorder or anticardiolipin syndrome; known hypersensitivity to nitinol or its components (nickel, titanium); known allergy to contrast or anesthetic drug despite premedication; anatomy that does not permit passage or deployment of the stent; active bacterial infection; a pre-existing stent at the target transverse-sigmoid sinus; and renal insufficiency not on dialysis.

locators: PDF page 19, Table 17 Stent Sizes
text: The River Stent is supplied in three sizes, all 70 mm long and tapered: SRS70-0910 (proximal 10.5 mm, distal 9.0 mm, distal perimeter 25 mm), SRS70-0708 (proximal 8.0 mm, distal 7.0 mm, distal perimeter 20 mm), and SRS70-0608 (proximal 8.0 mm, distal 6.0 mm, distal perimeter 17 mm).

locators: PDF page 19, section 10.2 Stent Size Selection
text: Size selection per labeling: measure the perimeter of the transverse sinus at its upstream third (the landing zone of the distal end of the stent) on pre-treatment MR venography, CT venography, or 3D catheter venography, and select the stent whose distal perimeter is immediately larger than the measured sinus perimeter (Table 17); appropriate size selection is required for wall apposition.

locators: PDF page 18, section 10.1 Required Materials
text: Labeling lists the required adjunctive materials: an introducer sheath of minimum 6F with minimum inner diameter 0.078 in (2 mm); a guide catheter of minimum 6F with minimum inner diameter 0.070 in (1.778 mm); an exchange-length (>300 cm) 0.014 in (0.36 mm) guidewire with a J-shaped tip; a microcatheter with minimum inner diameter 0.017 in; and a 5-10 cc saline flushing syringe.

locators: PDF page 5-6, section 5 Warnings, bullets on resistance and repositioning
text: Labeling warns not to reposition the River Stent in the transverse-sigmoid sinus: once deployment has started the stent must be entirely deployed; if unusual resistance is felt during access, the stent and delivery catheter are to be removed as a single unit.

locators: PDF page 6, section 6 Precautions
text: Labeling states that appropriate antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy should be administered before insertion of the River Stent System, and recommends a soft-tip J-shaped guidewire to avoid involuntary catheterization of a cortical vein during sinus catheterization and over-the-wire exchange.

locators: PDF page 6-7, section 7 Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) Safety Information
text: The River Stent is MR Conditional: 1.5 T or 3.0 T static field, maximum spatial field gradient 40 T/m (4,000 gauss/cm), circularly polarized RF excitation with no transmit-coil restriction, Normal Operating Mode, whole-body averaged SAR 2 W/kg for 60 minutes of continuous RF exposure; the implant produces an imaging artifact and may create susceptibility artifacts on MR venography that degrade assessment of lumen patency.

locators: PDF page 5 (English section), Indications for Use
text: US labeling indicates the Zilver Vascular Stent as an adjunct to percutaneous transluminal angioplasty in the treatment of symptomatic vascular disease of the iliac arteries up to 100 mm in length with a reference vessel diameter of 5 to 9 mm, in patients who are suitable candidates for PTA and/or stent treatment. The labeling does not address venous sinus or intracranial use.

locators: PDF page 5 (English section), Contraindications and Warnings
text: The labeling states there are no contraindications known at this time based on the clinical data; it warns that persons allergic to nitinol (nickel titanium) may suffer an allergic reaction to the implant.

locators: PDF page 5 (English section), Device Description size matrix
text: The Zilver Vascular Stent is available in outer diameters of 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 mm and lengths of 20, 30, 40, 60, and 80 mm, each preloaded on 5 French (1.67 mm), 6 French (2.0 mm), or 7 French (2.3 mm) delivery systems; hand-loading is not possible.

locators: PDF page 15 (English section), Table 10 Stent Size Selection Table
text: Table 10 size selection: reference vessel diameter 5.0 mm -> 6.0 mm nominal stent; 5.0-6.0 mm -> 7.0 mm; 6.0-7.0 mm -> 8.0 mm; 7.0-8.0 mm -> 9.0 mm; 8.0-9.0 mm -> 10.0 mm.

locators: PDF page 15 (English section), Directions for Use step 2 and step 4
text: The 7.0 and 6.0 French (2.3 and 2.0 mm) delivery systems accept a 0.035 inch (0.89 mm) wire guide; the 5.0 French (1.67 mm) system accepts a 0.018 inch (0.46 mm) wire guide; an extra- or ultra-stiff wire guide is specified and predilatation is recommended.

locators: PDF page 7 (English section), MR Conditional
text: The Zilver Vascular Stent is MR Conditional per non-clinical testing: static field 3 Tesla or less, spatial gradient 720 gauss/cm or less, whole-body averaged SAR 1.5 W/kg for 20 minutes (single stent at 1.5 T) and 3 W/kg for 15 minutes (single stent at 3 T, or overlapping stents at 1.5 and 3 T); maximum temperature rises of 0.1-3.8 degrees C were observed under those conditions.
